source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 6 (i)-(ii) (book p.275). (ii) asks to show a right triangle but P, Q, R form none; the key (PDF 312) agrees; correction callout.

blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Show that the vectors \(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) and \(2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) form a right triangle.
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do baatein saabit karni hain: pehli, teeno vectors waqai ek triangle banate hain; doosri, us triangle ka ek angle 90 degree hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen vectors.
Rule kaunsa? Triangle ke liye ek vector baqi do ka jama ho; right angle ke liye kisi jore ka dot product zero ho.
Plan: pehle jama check karein, phir teeno jore ke dot products.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{a} = 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{c} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\).
Saabit karna hai: yeh right triangle banate hain.
Tareeqa: Teen vectors triangle ki sides tabhi ban sakte hain jab head to tail rakhne par shakal band ho jaye, yani ek vector baqi do ke jama ke barabar ho. Phir right angle dhoondne ke liye dot product: jis jore ka dot product zero, un do sides ke beech 90 degree.

Triangle banta hai
\[\underline{b} + \underline{c} = (1 + 2)\underline{i} + (-3 + 1)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (5 - 4)\underline{k}\]
\[= 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k} = \underline{a}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{b}\) ke aakhri sire se \(\underline{c}\) shuru karein (head to tail). Triangle law ke mutabiq \(\underline{b}\) ke shuru se \(\underline{c}\) ke aakhir tak ka vector \(\underline{b} + \underline{c}\) hai, aur yeh bilkul \(\underline{a}\) hai. Is liye teeno sides mil kar band shakal yani triangle banati hain.

Zero dot product dhoondein
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b} = 3 + 6 + 5 = 14\]
\[\underline{b}\cdot\underline{c} = 2 - 3 - 20 = -21\]
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{c} = 6 - 2 - 4 = 0\]
Kyun: Teeno jore check kiye. Sirf \(\underline{a}\) aur \(\underline{c}\) ka dot product zero aaya, is liye yehi do sides perpendicular hain aur right angle inke beech hai.
Dhyan dein: Ek jora zero aate hi ruk sakte hain, lekin baqi do bhi dekh lena acha hai taa ke pata chale right angle kahan hai.

Tasdeeq: Pythagoras se
\[|\underline{a}|^2 = 14,\ |\underline{b}|^2 = 35,\ |\underline{c}|^2 = 21\]
\[|\underline{a}|^2 + |\underline{c}|^2 = 14 + 21\]
\[= 35 = |\underline{b}|^2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Right triangle mein hypotenuse (right angle ke saamne wali side, yahan \(\underline{b}\)) ka square baqi do sides ke squares ke jama ke barabar hota hai. Yeh bhi poora hua, to jawab pakka hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\underline{b} + \underline{c} = \underline{a}\), is liye triangle banta hai, aur \(\underline{a}\cdot\underline{c} = 0\), is liye yeh right triangle hai (right angle \(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\) aur \(2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) ke beech).

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Show that the set of points \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\) and \(R(-2, 4, 6)\) form a right triangle.
blocks.explanation:
Kisi vertex par right angle tab hota hai jab us vertex se nikalne wali dono sides ka dot product zero ho.
Diya kya hai? Teen points.
Karna kya hai? Har vertex par angle test karna.
Plan: teeno side vectors, teeno vertices par dot product, phir faisla. (Yaad rahe: yahan kitab ka sawal hi ghalat nikalta hai, neeche dekhiye.)
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\), \(R(-2, 4, 6)\).
Dekhna hai: kya \(PQR\) right triangle hai?
Tareeqa: Side vectors 'head minus tail' se banayenge, phir \(P\), \(Q\) aur \(R\) teeno par dot product dekhenge. Right angle kisi bhi vertex par ho sakta hai, is liye teeno check karna zaroori hai.

Side vectors
\[\underline{PQ} = -3\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{QR} = -3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 7\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{PR} = -6\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\]
Kyun: Maslan \(\underline{PQ} = (1 - 4, 3 - (-1), -1 - 2) = (-3, 4, -3)\). Har dafa head ke coordinates mein se tail ke coordinates minus kiye.

\(P\) par angle
\[\underline{PQ}\cdot\underline{PR} = 18 + 20 - 12\]
\[= 26 \ne 0\]
Kyun: \(P\) se nikalne wali sides \(\underline{PQ}\) aur \(\underline{PR}\) hain. \((-3)(-6) = 18\), \(4 \times 5 = 20\), \((-3)(4) = -12\). Zero nahi, to \(P\) par right angle nahi.

\(Q\) par angle
\[\underline{QP} = 3\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{QP}\cdot\underline{QR} = -9 - 4 + 21\]
\[= 8 \ne 0\]
Kyun: \(Q\) wale angle ke liye dono vectors \(Q\) se shuru hone chahiye, is liye \(\underline{PQ}\) ki jagah us ka ulta \(\underline{QP}\) liya. Zero nahi aaya.

\(R\) par angle
\[\underline{RP} = 6\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{RQ} = 3\underline{i} - \underline{j} - 7\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{RP}\cdot\underline{RQ} = 18 + 5 + 28\]
\[= 51 \ne 0\]
Kyun: \(R\) se nikalne wale dono vectors liye. Yeh bhi zero nahi.

Natija aur tasdeeq
\[|PQ|^2 = 34,\ |QR|^2 = 59,\ |PR|^2 = 77\]
\[34 + 59 = 93 \ne 77\]
Kyun: Teeno vertices par dot product zero nahi, balke teeno positive hain, yani teeno angles acute hain. Pythagoras bhi sab se lambi side ke liye poora nahi hota. Is liye yeh triangle right triangle nahi hai; kitab ka 'show that' wala sawal saabit nahi kiya ja sakta.
blocks.final_answer: Yeh saabit nahi ho sakta: \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) triangle to banate hain magar is mein koi right angle nahi (dot products 26, 8, 51).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab kehti hai ke saabit karo \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\), \(R(-2, 4, 6)\) right triangle banate hain. Yeh ghalat hai: \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) par dot products 26, 8 aur 51 hain, koi bhi zero nahi. Kitab ki apni answer key (PDF 312) bhi yehi kehti hai ke yeh points right triangle nahi banate, aur woh sahi hai. Exam mein teeno dot products dikha kar yehi natija likhiye.
